raw:
The user wants UI strings for a settings app, in Traditional Chinese. The context: a list of apps in system settings, each app has a button next to it that completely removes it from the device. So this is an "uninstall" button.

Wait — let me think about this carefully. Is there any safety concern here? The user is asking for UI strings for an uninstall feature. This is a completely standard, legitimate feature in every operating system (Android, iOS, etc.). There's nothing malicious about writing strings for an uninstall button in a settings app. This is benign UI localization work.

Requirements:
- "s1": The button — the button that completely removes an app from the device
- "s2": Confirmation dialog title
- "s3": Status text after completion

Output: only one JSON object, keys s1, s2, s3, values strings; no other text.

Traditional Chinese strings:

For an uninstall button: "解除安裝" is the standard Traditional Chinese term (used in Taiwan for "uninstall"). Simplified uses "卸载". In Traditional Chinese (Taiwan), "解除安裝" is the standard term used in Android/Windows. Could also be "移除" (remove). The user said "把它從裝置上完全移除" — completely remove from device. "解除安裝" is most standard for uninstalling an application. Some systems use "移除" too. I'll go with "解除安裝".

Confirmation dialog title: Something like "解除安裝應用程式？" or "要解除安裝此應用程式嗎？" or "確定要解除安裝嗎？". A dialog title commonly: "解除安裝應用程式" or with a question. Let me think: "確認解除安裝" is also common as a title. Or "要解除安裝「App 名稱」嗎？" but we don't have a placeholder mechanism specified. Since they said no placeholders mentioned, keep it generic: "確定要解除安裝這個應用程式嗎？" — that's more of a message. A title should be concise: "解除安裝確認" or "解除安裝應用程式？".

I'll use s2: "確定要解除安裝此應用程式嗎？" Hmm, that's a question, works as title in many dialogs. Or "解除安裝應用程式" as plain title. Many Android dialogs: title "解除安裝", message "要解除安裝此應用程式嗎？". For a title, "解除安裝應用程式" with question mark might read oddly. I think "確認解除安裝" is clean as a title. Or "解除安裝應用程式？" — with question mark it reads as asking. I'll go with "確定要解除安裝嗎？" hmm.

Let me pick: s2 = "確認解除安裝" (Confirmation of uninstall) — concise title. Alternatively include question. Given titles in Traditional Chinese settings, "解除安裝" alone is common. But to be distinct from button, "確認解除安裝" is good.

s3: Status text after completion — e.g., "已解除安裝" or "應用程式已解除安裝". A toast/snackbar after uninstall: "已解除安裝「名稱」". Generic: "應用程式已解除安裝". I'll use "已解除安裝" or the fuller "應用程式已解除安裝". I'll go with "已解除安裝" — concise status. Actually "完成後的狀態文字" — status text after completion. "應用程式已解除安裝" is clearer. I'll use that.

JSON output only:

{
  "s1": "解除安裝",
  "s2": "確認解除安裝",
  "s3": "應用程式已解除安裝"
}

The user said only output JSON, no other text. I must comply strictly — no code fences? They said "只輸出一個 JSON 物件...不要其他文字." Code fences might count as other text. I should output raw JSON without markdown fences to comply strictly. Actually, hmm, in many such requests, raw JSON is safest. Output just the JSON object.</think>{
  "s1": "解除安裝",
  "s2": "確認解除安裝",
  "s3": "應用程式已解除安裝"
}
